svg.title: Where business meaning is stored in each project
svg.desc: Four rows, one per project. Wren AI stores meaning in MDL, a versioned JSON manifest of models, relationships, cubes and metrics held in the repository and reviewed in pull requests. DB-GPT stores it across AWEL flow definitions, retrieved knowledge and agent configuration, which is partly declarative and partly operational. Vanna stores it as an accumulated corpus of question and SQL pairs retrieved at query time, which is data rather than a document. Dataherald stores it as golden SQL examples and schema instructions inside its own services. Only the first is something a data team can diff and approve before it reaches the model.
svg.text: The artefact between the question and the SQL
MDL — a JSON manifest of models, columns, relationships,
views, cubes and metrics, held in the repository.
AWEL flow definitions, retrieved knowledge and agent
configuration, spread across a wider data-agent runtime.
An accumulated corpus of DDL, docs and question–SQL
pairs, retrieved at query time from a vector store.
Cheap to start. Not a document anyone owns.
Golden SQL examples and schema instructions held inside
its own services, behind an API-first orchestration layer.
Explicit examples, but coupled to the runtime.
The output is the same query. The difference is whether the definition it encodes was ever approved by a person.
